title: Catalogue publisher-identity and namespace-squatting defenses that a one-owner registry can run
question: Which identity and namespace defenses (scoped names, verified publishers, reserved prefixes, typo-distance blocking) are implementable by a single-owner marketplace with no review staff, and which fundamentally require human moderation?
answer: Split each named defense into the part a computer can enforce and the part that is a judgment. Scoped names are automatable as an account-owned prefix ACL (npm grants @scope at signup); they do not stop brand-scope squatting. 'Verified publishers' is two different controls: OIDC trusted publishing is automatable cryptography and does not attest a legal entity; VS Code/NuGet identity badges require staff reputation and identifying-question review. Reserved prefixes are automatable as a 409 prefix ACL *after* a grant exists (PEP 752 / NuGet); issuing the grant (PEP 755 harm/identity criteria, PEP 541 workgroup, crates.io squat takedowns) is moderation-dependent. Typo-distance blocking is automatable for Warehouse ultranormalize collisions; TypoSnyper in the captured source is an admin observation after create and is not a gate. A one-owner prompt-payload marketplace can ship D1, D2, D4, D6 with no review staff. It cannot honestly ship D3, D5, or D7 without hiring moderators or accepting that those rows are theatre.

control.why: A table that classified every defense automatable would deny PEP 755 independent review, VS Code's 5-day reputation check, and TypoSnyper's admin-only observation. That classification would not be honest.

defense_table.reason: Binding a prefix to an account is a membership check. npm grants a scope that matches the user or organization name at signup; only members of that scope can publish into it. A one-owner marketplace implements the same rule as UNIQUE(owner_id, local_name) plus a publish ACL. No human is required to enforce the ACL once the scope exists. It does not, by itself, stop someone from registering an unused brand scope first.

defense_table.reason: Trusted publishing exchanges a short-lived OIDC token from a named IdP (GitHub Actions, GitLab, CircleCI) against a preconfigured trust policy. Verification is cryptographic (JWT signature + claims). PyPI, npm, and the OpenSSF trusted-publishers profile all describe this as an automated publisher-to-CI binding. It does not prove that the package author is a named legal entity. npm does not even verify the saved configuration until publish time.

defense_table.defense: reserved prefixes (enforcement after a grant exists)
defense_table.reason: Once a grant exists, PEP 752 requires uploads matching the reserved namespace to fail with HTTP 409 unless the uploader holds the grant. NuGet rejects submissions on a reserved ID prefix unless they come from the prefix owner. That is a string-prefix ACL a single owner can run with no staff. It does not decide who receives the grant.

defense_table.defense: reserved prefixes (who gets the grant / trademark / squat judgment)
defense_table.reason: Issuing the grant is a judgment: PEP 755 approval criteria include whether the namespace 'properly and clearly identify the reservation owner' and whether not reserving it 'may cause ambiguity, confusion, or other harm'. Applications 'require independent review'. PEP 541 name-retention disputes are tickets against pypi/support; the Packaging Workgroup has the final say. crates.io's RFC 3463 lets the team delete crates that exist only to squat a name. A staffless marketplace can seed a static well-known list; it cannot adjudicate competing claims.

evidence.claim: npm registry serves scoped package names of the form @scope/name
npm grants a matching scope at account or organization creation
ultranormalize similar-name check is a blocking raise in check_project_name
TypoSnyper is a post-create admin observation, not a lifecycle gate
reserved-namespace uploads MUST 409 without an active grant
prefix grant applications require independent human review
VS Code verified-publisher badge includes staff legitimacy review
PEP 541 name disputes exist as live human tickets

strongest_surviving_counterargument: A staffless operator could pretreat 'moderation-dependent' rows as automatable by publishing a frozen list of famous prefixes and a Levenshtein>=1 reject against the top-N names. That is a different and narrower control (static denylist + edit distance) than grant issuance or a verified-identity badge. The table already admits static lists as automatable; it refuses to relabel PEP 755 / VS Code reputation review as automatable just because a denylist exists.
